transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess what brings me in is my eating has started to feel really out of control, especially on late work nights. I’m a graphic designer, so sometimes I’m working way later than I mean to, and I’ll order food and tell myself it’s just dinner, like a normal dinner because I’m tired and I don’t want to cook. But then it becomes, you know, a full entrée, plus sides, and then dessert, and then after that I’ll still go into the kitchen and grab extra snacks.

And it’s just… it’s way more than I would ever eat if someone were sitting across from me watching or eating with me. I think that’s the part that’s been bothering me, because in the moment I sort of justify each thing, but afterward it’s like, “Why did I need all of that?” It doesn’t feel like a normal amount for me.
Can you tell me more about those times when you’re eating a lot—do you feel like you can stop at any time, or does it feel like you lose control once you start eating?

It feels like I lose control. Not right away every single time, like sometimes it starts with me thinking, okay, I’m choosing to order this, I’m hungry, I worked late, whatever. But then there’s this point where it changes, and I’m almost watching myself keep going.

Like I’ll be clicking back into the delivery app to add something else, or after the food is gone I’ll open a bag or a package in the kitchen, and part of me is very clearly thinking, you should stop now, this is enough. But it doesn’t feel like that thought actually does anything. It’s like the decision has already slipped out of my hands by then, and I’m just continuing even though I know I don’t really want to.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t think I do anything really extreme afterward, if that’s what you mean. Like, I don’t have some set thing where I’m like, “Now I have to fix it,” or anything that organized.

I do sometimes feel really uncomfortable afterward and ashamed, and I’ll think about how I shouldn’t eat like that again, or I’ll kind of make plans in my head to be more careful the next day. But in terms of making myself sick or taking something or doing some huge workout specifically to undo it… I don’t think that’s really been part of it for me. It’s more like I just sit with this awful, heavy feeling and tell myself I’ll do better, and then I sort of try to move on.
Do you ever feel like you eat even when you’re not hungry, or continue eating even after you’re full, because you feel like you can’t stop?

Yes. That’s actually a big part of what scares me about it. A lot of the time it’s not like I’m starving and then I overdo it. It can happen after I’ve already had what I would consider a normal dinner, like a real dinner where I should be done.

Then I’ll be working on a project late, kind of tired and still at my computer, and I’ll find myself wandering into the kitchen. Or I’ll open a delivery app even though, if I stopped and checked in with myself, I’m not physically hungry at all. It’s more like I’m restless or stuck in that work mode, and food becomes this thing I keep reaching for.

And then once I start, even if I’m full, I keep going. I’ll have this very clear thought of, “You’re not hungry, you already ate,” but it doesn’t seem to stop me in the moment. It feels really embarrassing to say because it sounds so simple, like just don’t get up or don’t order it, but when it’s happening it feels like I can’t quite interrupt it.
Do these episodes of eating happen more often when you’re feeling stressed, anxious, or down, or do they seem to happen more randomly, even when you’re feeling okay emotionally?

I’m not completely sure, honestly. I’ve tried to figure that out, because it would almost be easier if I could say, “Oh, this only happens when I’m upset,” and then I could point to a reason.

Sometimes it does seem connected to stress, especially if I’ve been working late or I feel kind of wound up and tired. But other times I don’t feel especially sad or anxious beforehand, at least not in some obvious way. I might just feel sort of… blank, or restless, or like I’m still mentally buzzing. And then suddenly I’m thinking about food or ordering something.

So I wouldn’t say it’s totally random, but I also can’t neatly tie it to one emotion every time. It’s more like I notice it after the fact and think, “What was that about?” rather than being able to predict it clearly.
How often do these episodes happen where you feel like you can’t stop eating, and do they happen even when you’re not physically hungry?

I think… when I actually look at it instead of just going by memory, it’s usually at least once a week. I didn’t realize that at first, because in my head I’d sort of tell myself it was “every now and then,” but when I’ve gone back through delivery receipts or looked at my calendar and thought about which nights got away from me, there’s pretty consistently one night a week where it happens. Sometimes it’s more than that, depending on the week.

And yes, it does happen when I’m not physically hungry. That’s part of why it feels so upsetting, because it’s not like I can always explain it as, “Well, I skipped dinner,” or something. A lot of the time I’ve already eaten, and then later I’m still ordering or snacking and I know I’m not hungry. That pattern has been going on for several months now, I’d say.
Do you feel a lot of distress or upset about these episodes of eating, like they’re interfering with how you see yourself or affecting your daily life?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I don’t have some neat measurement for it. It definitely bothers me, but I’m not sure where the line is between “I feel bad about something I did” and “this is really affecting my life,” if that makes sense.

After it happens, I usually feel pretty upset with myself. Not even just physically full, but like… disappointed, and kind of ashamed, honestly. I’ll think, “Why did I do that again?” And then I’ll replay the whole thing in my head, like if I had just closed my laptop earlier, or if I hadn’t opened the app, or if I’d gone to bed instead. It becomes this whole self-criticism loop.

I do think it affects how I see myself, because I start feeling like I’m someone with no discipline, which is really hard for me because in other parts of my life I’m pretty functional. I work, I meet deadlines, I take care of things. So then it feels confusing and embarrassing that with this one thing I feel so out of control.

As far as daily life… I don’t know. I still go to work and do what I need to do, so it’s not like everything stops. But it can make the next day feel heavier. I might wake up already irritated with myself, or distracted, or just not wanting to think about it. So yes, it upsets me, but I guess I’m still trying to understand how much it’s interfering.
During these episodes when you feel like you can’t stop eating, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual?

Yes. I think that’s actually one of the clearer parts of it. When it’s happening, I’m not eating in a normal way, like sitting down and having a meal and noticing it. It’s much faster than that.

A lot of the time I’m at my desk, with work still open — like Illustrator files on the screen — and I’ll have containers or packaging next to me, and I just sort of move from one thing to the next. It’s almost automatic. I’ll take a bite, then another, and I’m not really tasting it after the first few bites. I’m just… continuing.

Then there’s this moment where I kind of come back to myself and realize most of it is already gone, and it’s only been a few minutes. That part feels really strange, because if you asked me what it tasted like or whether I enjoyed it, I don’t know that I could even answer properly. It’s more like I was trying to get through it, not enjoy it.
During these episodes when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you're not in control of yourself, like you're just going through the motions and can't stop even though you want to?

Yes… that’s exactly what it feels like. Not the whole time, maybe, because at the beginning there’s usually some part of me that knows I’m choosing to start. But once I start, there’s this point where it changes, where I’m almost watching myself keep going.

Like I’ll click back to the food, or open another package, or keep reaching for something, and in my head I’m thinking, “You should stop now. This is enough. You’re not even enjoying this anymore.” But my body just keeps doing it anyway. It feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands by then.

And that’s the part that scares me or makes me feel really ashamed afterward, because it’s not like I don’t know what I’m doing. I do know. I can see it happening. I can be thinking very clearly that I don’t want to keep going, and still I keep going through the motions. It feels automatic, like I’m just along for the ride until it’s over.
